status: The keyword canon: page types with their lexicons (title / body / ambiguous terms), codeability and path. Paths are in the page taxonomy's names (page_taxonomy.json), put there by `python -m stages.lib.page_classify.canon_convert` (see paths_from). Lexicons are starting lists or the page type's own name: tune them on labelled pages.
how_to_match: Match case-insensitively on whole words or whole phrases, never on substrings of a longer word.
Longest match wins: when one term is contained in a longer term that also matched at the same place, count only the longer one.
title_terms are names a document prints as its title or main heading. They count more when found in the title zone (the first lines of the page).
A single-word title term counts as a title hit only when it is a heading on its own line, not when it appears inside a sentence.
body_terms are supporting words found in the body of that kind of page.

ambiguous_terms are short abbreviations, generic words, or terms shared by more than one page type. They add to a score only when another term of the same sub-type has already matched; they never decide a page alone.

Score each sub-type, take the best sub-type per page type as that page type's score, and report the top page type, its best sub-type, the score, the margin over the second page type, and whether a title term hit in the title zone.

codeability_rules.context: depends on the document the page is bound into (continuity); needs_review until then
codeability_rules.source: depends on the ingest source, which is not on the page; needs_review until supplied
